method: Full roots and actual connected paths read manually from pinned Git. Metadata-only serialization of explicit reviewed line spans; no source parser/scanner or source execution. Declaration bytes from func through column-zero close excluding following LF. Assertion spans retain the full root interior, including every assertion and its conditions. All baseline/current mapped declarations match survival hashes; only non-root added test shifts parse root current line by11.

classification_definitions.integration: Genuine production file/store/service/protocol boundary materially supports asserted observable behavior.
classification_definitions.unit: Local validation, handler/serialization or synthetic feeds; incidental setup alone gives no boundary credit.
classification_definitions.mixed: Separate independent boundary assertions and local-only assertions in one root.
classification_definitions.unresolved: Missing/ambiguous source or accounting evidence; distinct from runtime UNKNOWN.

roots.reason: NewLogger writes its unprefixed JSON record to a real os.File; output.String reads that same path. The asserted bytes are observed across the production log sink/file boundary; journald selection is stubbed, so no real journal integration is claimed.

Production slog handler writes both formats to the real process.log sink and the assertion reads the persisted bytes to check UTC record time and preserved attribute zone. The fixed input clock is synthetic; the asserted output crosses the actual file sink.

The long stat bytes replace the fixture file and production readSystem opens and reads it before parseProcStat returns the observed CPU count/user seconds. This directly exercises the production proc-file read boundary; it does not inspect the live host proc filesystem.

Both truncated-provider and capped-database blocks scrape the real project Server with a loopback HTTP client. Collector registry writers render the injected views in the actual response body. Providers are synthetic; no NATS or TerraBase observation is claimed.

Append, Export, Import and HistoryHandler are in-memory operations. gzip encodes to bytes.Buffer, Import reads bytes.Reader, and ServeHTTP writes a recorder. No KVHistorySnapshots Save/Load, filesystem or network boundary is reached despite the root name.

The metrics output assertions at lines 31–45 traverse collectorHTTP loopback TCP. Independent history/sampler assertions at 46–73 use memory and direct HistoryHandler recorder; the final JSON null/truncation assertion at 75–78 is local serialization. These distinct unit blocks make this root mixed.

Fixed snapshot/cluster providers return synthetic structs. Remounting and direct ServeHTTP recorder assertions exercise local atomic source replacement, mux registration and JSON encoding; no listener/client/store boundary supports the asserted replacement.

NewServer reaches readBearerToken os.Open/file.Stat on the actual chmod0644 file and rejects its observed permission metadata. The filesystem permission boundary directly supports the security assertion.

The token file is setup for a handler whose requests use direct recorders. Health callback, event ring and registry counter are in-process inputs; assertions target route/auth/header/method decisions and serialization, with no network or persistent-state effect/readback.
Start rejects the tokenless non-loopback address at its local pre-listen guard; net.Listen is never reached on the asserted path.

Production Server.Start binds TCP and serves net/http; http.Get reads the actual /metrics response including real process metrics. Cancellation observes the listener serve result through production Close. The earlier port probe only chooses an address.

The positive listener table uses NewServer plus direct recorder dispatch; the token file is incidental setup. Invalid addresses are rejected by ValidateListenAddress before listening, and invalid configs by Config.Validate. No asserted socket bind or token-file metadata transition occurs.
Each Host case reaches local ServeHTTP/LiteralHost and direct recorder output. There is no DNS lookup, listener or real HTTP client exchange; the custom extra handler is in-process.

Issuance commits a real JetStream KV allocation, then an injected leader timeout blocks generation read. The HTTP recorder response is paired with real leader readback proving cleanup or preservation of a later reused revision. Hook delegates KV Create before injecting the read outage.

Lost acknowledgments follow delegated real KV Create. Read/purge outage hooks temporarily prevent reconciliation; restored methods plus production listener-owned retry cleanup reconcile real entries. Real readback verifies removal/preserved concurrent reused slots; hook deadline/map observations constrain this same cleanup scenario.

Multiple actual production server session managers share one real loopback JetStream store. Registration CAS, leader reads, issuance, revocation and status/readback establish stale-version refusal, signed-reference fences, rotation and binding reconciliation. Version descriptors are synthetic: no Vault/signature service is exercised.

Create hook first delegates real JetStream Create, then cancels the request. Production rollback uses its independent bounded context to purge the committed allocation; a fresh leader read asserts absence, including absence of a purge marker.

After real session creation, injected Watch failure interrupts only enumeration. Rotation commits via real KV Update before old-session validation; fresh issuance/reattachment use the actual shared store. Restored Watch and Status verify deferred collection. Failure hook is not a substitute store.

The root puts old-form metadata in a real JetStream KV and calls SetSessionStore, whose authoritative read rejects it. A fresh leader read proves the exact invalid bytes remained unchanged. The rejection is local decoding of boundary-delivered data, not a detached parser assertion.

Real KV allocation is canceled after delegated Create. Injected stream purge timeout leaves a retry obligation; production listener cleanup later retries with the real stream. Actual leader readback proves removal or preservation/validity of a later reused slot. Deadline/map checks observe this same boundary-driven rollback.

qualification_limits: SOURCE_ONLY_CANDIDATE. Runtime UNKNOWN_NO_RECEIPTS_REVIEWED_NO_EXECUTION; no compilation or test execution.

The session fixture starts upstream NATS directly and connects over loopback TCP. It does not call natscell.Start, use production TLS/JWT, validate distributed replication or qualify live Vault/signatures.
Fault hooks delegate specified real operations then inject timeout/cancellation, or replace only enumeration/read/purge methods as cited. No simulated outage is claimed as an actual network failure.
Collector views are injected. Real loopback HTTP proves response wiring/rendering, not live NATS route measurement or TerraBase runtime correctness.
File sink and proc fixture scenarios cross real local file reads/writes; no actual journald, live /proc host observation, crash durability or production filesystem qualification is inferred.
Direct HTTP recorders and byte-buffer history roundtrips have no independent service/network/store credit.
No repository/shared-ledger change, source/test deletion, retirement, runtime qualification, global completion or count promotion is authorized. All safety obligations retained.
